bullets.title: Fed likely needs 50-100bp of additional hikes; 1999-2000 analog points to +50bp in 10Y yields
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags the real Fed funds rate fell to 0.4% in June — the lowest since April 2023 — suggesting policy is no longer restrictive. Using the June 1999–May 2000 hiking cycle as the best analog, they model a 50bp rise in intermediate Treasuries and 30bp flattening in the 5s/30s curve. JPMorgan also flags their mid-year global outlook expects Fed hikes despite falling oil prices, with core CPI expected to exceed 3% in 2026.

bullets.title: May PCE in line at 0.3% m/m / 3.4% y/y; super-core services running hot at +0.5%
bullets.body: Headline PCE came in at 0.3% m/m in line with consensus; core goods fell 0.1% but super-core services surged 0.5% m/m — the key sticking point. Chicago Fed President Goolsbee noted core inflation is "still too high and trending wrong way." Hedgeye's June CPI nowcast sits at +3.85% y/y (-40bp sequentially), with the official read due July 14.

bullets.title: MU blowout drives AI capex trade revival; semis +3.6% while hardware worst sub-sector at -3.7%
bullets.body: Micron delivered a blowout F3Q with 16 strategic customer agreements (SCAs) featuring take-or-pay volume commitments and pricing floors above prior peak gross margins; management expects tight supply to persist beyond 2027. Semis outperformed +3.6% on the session; MU briefly eclipsed Meta and Tesla in market cap. Conversely, hardware was the worst IT sub-sector (-3.7%) as Apple's 15-25% MacBook/iPad price hikes — blamed on memory input costs — sent AAPL down ~6%.

bullets.title: Mag 7 as source of funds for cyclical rotation; equal-weight S&P outpaced cap-weight by ~70bp
bullets.body: Equal-weight S&P 500 outpaced the cap-weighted index by roughly 70bp on the session as Mag 7 weakness — four names down double-digits YTD 2026 — provided the funding. Small caps, industrials, builders, travel & leisure, and banks were standouts. 22V flags MSFT specifically: Technical Score 0, below deteriorating 200-day MA since February, approaching March lows with downside risk to $250 if $350 support breaks.

bullets.title: Capital markets activity surging: equity issuance +110% YoY, IPOs ~5x, M&A +60% YoY in 2Q26
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Deal Dashboard shows 2Q26 shaping up as the strongest capital markets quarter in years: equity issuance tracking +110% y/y led by North America at +208%, IPOs nearly 5x y/y, and announced M&A +60% y/y. Sponsor M&A is broadening with activity accelerating to +10% y/y, and completed M&A sponsor volume up 53% y/y vs. strategics at +10%.

bullets.title: Benign disinflation base case supports banks, biotech, cyclicals — but momentum vulnerable if core PCE stays above ~0.2%/month
bullets.body: The base case remains a soft-landing disinflation path that extends the economic cycle rather than triggering a Fed-tightening recession. This backdrop is constructive for banks, biotech, and cyclicals. However, falling inflation expectations, a stronger USD, and weaker gold alone are insufficient to signal a durable risk-asset rally — momentum remains fragile if core PCE readings stay elevated.

bullets.title: 10Y yield below 4.40% (5-week low); rates lower on the week despite hawkish macro backdrop
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.40% — the lowest since early May — providing a tailwind to cyclicals and rate-sensitive names even as macro data supports further Fed tightening. The move lower comes despite PCE printing in-line and Fed officials flagging sticky inflation, suggesting some dovish positioning unwind or technical factors at play.

bullets.title: Iran attacked Singapore-flagged vessel in Strait of Hormuz; markets largely shrugging off geopolitical noise
bullets.body: An IRGC projectile incident on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz was reported, but markets mostly disregarded the event given the partial normalization of Persian Gulf crude exports (back to ~75% of pre-war levels with ~13M barrels in region) and a US-Iran peace agreement in progress. WTI crude was up 2.3% on the day after a 3.5% decline Wednesday; energy prices remain ~18% above pre-conflict levels but retail fuel is down ~5% month-over-month.

bullets.title: 1Q26 US real GDP revised up to +2.1% annualized; capex broadening beyond tech with machinery/metals at record highs
bullets.body: First-quarter real GDP was revised up 0.5pp to 2.1% q/q annualized on stronger trade and capex. Real capex revised up 50bp to +10.6%; tech orders +0.3% m/m and tech shipments surged 2% m/m. Importantly, the capex cycle is broadening beyond tech — machinery and fabricated metals orders reached record highs, supporting the cyclical/broadening trade thesis.

bullets.title: JPM mid-year outlook: cyclical upturn sustained in 2H26; tech spend broadening beyond hyperscalers
bullets.body: JPMorgan's 2026 mid-year global economic outlook calls for continued above-potential growth driven by the tech boom (AI spending broadening beyond hyperscalers), fading business caution lifting investment, and the Strait of Hormuz re-opening reducing energy shock risk. US job growth seen sustaining 100k+/month; Brent projected at $80/bbl in 2H26. More aggressive central bank action cited as the key tail risk.

bullets.title: US midterm primaries: macro policy vectors (tariffs, deregulation, geopolitics) likely unchanged regardless of outcome
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's pulse check on midterms (~50% of primaries completed) finds Democratic enthusiasm advantage in early data but concludes that key macro policy drivers — tariffs, geopolitics, deregulation — are likely to persist across election outcomes. A 'fragile' Democratic majority would produce policy noise but divided government wouldn't derail variables under executive control.

bullets.title: Upcoming macro catalysts: NFP Jul 2, ISM-Mfg Jul 1, USMCA review begins Jul 1, Fed meets Jul 29
bullets.body: Key events next week: China PMI Jun 29, ISM-Mfg Jul 1, USMCA six-year formal joint review kicks off Jul 1, NFP Jul 2, and June CPI Jul 14. Fed meetings scheduled for Jul 29 and Sep 16. Xi potential visit to US in 2H26; US-China trade truce expires Nov 1.

bullets.title: onsemi acquires Synaptics in $7B all-stock deal; 1.35 ON shares per SYNA share, $200M synergy target
bullets.body: onsemi agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock transaction valued at ~$7B ($125.62/share). SYNA holders receive 1.350 ON shares per share (~12% pro-forma ownership). The deal is expected to be accretive to non-GAAP EPS within 18 months with $200M annual synergies; closing targeted mid-2027.

bullets.title: AI enterprise budget pressure: cheaper open-source and Chinese model alternatives gaining traction
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Tech Talk podcast highlights enterprise customers increasingly evaluating cost vs. value on AI workloads, with open-source and Chinese model alternatives (despite security concerns) pressuring incumbents. Orchestration and model-routing layers are emerging as a potential hedge. Jevon's Paradox is cited as a demand multiplier even as per-unit costs fall. Separately, Alibaba was accused by Anthropic of large-scale distillation to illicitly access Claude capabilities.

bullets.title: Container shipping costs rising, signaling building core goods price pressure despite crude decline
bullets.body: JPMorgan's energy shock monitor flags container shipping costs moving notably higher — a leading indicator of goods inflation — even as retail fuel prices fell ~1.8% week-over-week. US gasoline is still up 32% vs. pre-conflict levels, and jet-fuel prices continue to lag Brent's move lower, suggesting goods and travel inflation may stay elevated in near-term CPI prints.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR surging: weekly +9.7% YoY; luxury +17.4%, World Cup boosting top-25 markets +15.5%
bullets.body: For the week of June 14-20, US hotel RevPAR was up 9.7% y/y (vs. +7.0% prior week) driven by ADR +8.4% and occupancy +81bps; luxury led at +17.4%. The first full week of World Cup data is a notable driver — San Francisco +80.5%, Houston +28.1%, Las Vegas +26.2%. Trailing 28-day RevPAR now up +7.3% y/y.

bullets.title: Comcast Sky nearing ~$2.2B ITV M&E acquisition; Paramount-WBD merger progressing toward EU approval
bullets.body: Comcast's Sky unit is reportedly nearing an agreement to acquire ITV's Media & Entertainment business for ~$2.2B to strengthen UK streaming. Separately, the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger is progressing with EU approval likely but a UK regulatory hurdle remaining. Advertising segment was down 3.1% on the session with APP leading declines.

bullets.title: Memory cost inflation driving hardware price hikes; AAPL and MSFT raising consumer hardware prices
bullets.body: Apple announced 15-25% price increases on MacBooks and iPads citing rapid data center expansion driving memory/storage demand shortages, and is skipping the M6 chip to jump directly to an AI-focused M7. Microsoft is raising Xbox Series console prices worldwide (third increase) starting August 1. Both moves reflect AI capex-driven input cost inflation flowing through to consumer hardware pricing.

bullets.title: Capex broadening trade: semis, industrials, oil services leading; China Internet and unprofitable tech lagging
bullets.body: Into the close, NDX futures led SPX and RTY while Mag 7 lagged all three major indices. Semis and oil services led sector performance; industrials outperformed within SPX. China Internet and unprofitable tech were the primary laggards. The rotation into cyclicals/value/small caps is consistent with the broadening narrative supported by the capex data revisions and MU's SCA pricing disclosures.

bullets.title: Las Vegas airport traffic +8.4% YoY in May; Louisiana casino GGR +8% YoY with CZR outperforming at +24%
bullets.body: Las Vegas Harry Reid airport traffic rose 8.4% y/y in May (+4.4% m/m), signaling strong gaming destination demand. Louisiana statewide casino GGR of $246M was up 8% y/y, with CZR's Louisiana portfolio surging 22.8% y/y (Harrah's New Orleans +29%, Horseshoe Bossier City +39%) — well ahead of JPM's +3% forecast — while PENN tracked at +3% y/y.
